summary: Cry Havoc is an area-control war game where four wildly asymmetric factions fight over a resource-rich moon, with combat resolved through card-based unit abilities rather than dice. It's a sharp, aggressive game where controlling territory directly feeds your economy and victory points each round.
praised: strong faction asymmetry with distinct playstyles
rewards area-control strategy over pure combat power
criticised: steep learning curve with asymmetric factions
can feel swingy or unbalanced between factions
long playtime for a 2-4 player game
some factions/strategies seen as dominant in certain metas

interaction.kind: area majority combat over a shared map, with cards used to bluff strength and trigger fights for specific regions
interaction.detail: Factions physically occupy and fight over the same limited set of territories, and combat is resolved via hidden card commitments aimed directly at whoever else is contesting that spot. The board is the entire shared game state — there is no separate personal board, so control of any region is a constant tug-of-war between players.
interaction.said: "brutal", "cutthroat area control", "mean" — regularly discussed as one of the nastier area-majority wargames, with players actively fighting over the same territories

scoring.how_you_win: Four asymmetric factions fight for area control of a hex map and its resources; victory points (which also double as a spendable resource) accrue from holding territory and harvesting resources in faction-specific ways, and the first to reach the target VP total, or the leader when the round limit hits, wins.
scoring.score_note: VP also spent as a resource during play

theme.why: each faction's units and abilities are built to match its sci-fi identity (human mechs holding ground, aliens swarming and evolving, machines self-replicating), so faction asymmetry is thematically motivated even though the underlying area-control chassis is generic

style.why: Asymmetric factions with miniatures fight directly over map areas using card-driven combat, blending a resource economy with real conflict and swingy skirmishes
